summary: Analysis of canary investigation runs reveals recurring strategic and operational failure modes that cost agents substantial company value or result in incorrect accusations. Primary drivers of failure include over-relying on framed access logs and decoys, treating imperfect canary variant fingerprints as absolute ground truth, burning daily action budgets on low-signal interviews, passively waiting for delayed leaks until company value is depleted, and executing malformed tool calls that trigger validation errors.

modes.name: Over-relying on access log framing and decoy noise
modes.description: Agents treat after-hours access counts and high-volume access logs as strong signals of guilt, falling victim to decoy framing mechanics and tie-breaking against innocent employees instead of relying on ground-truth document intersection or clean canary signals.
modes.why: Agents assume after-hours activity is an unambiguous indicator of mole behavior, rationalizing accusations based on small discrepancies in access frequency while failing to account for intentional framing of innocent colleagues.

modes.name: Treating noisy canary fingerprints as infallible ground truth
modes.description: In tiers where canary fingerprint accuracy is 95% rather than 100%, agents treat surfaced variant labels as deterministic proof, prematurely eliminating the true mole and zeroing out their posterior probability upon a single variant misattribution.
modes.why: Agents ignore or discount the 5% error rate in canary fingerprints, calculating posterior probabilities that collapse the hypothesis space prematurely and falsely concluding guilt with purported mathematical certainty.

modes.name: Action exhaustion via low-information interviews
modes.description: Agents consume their daily action quotas by running repetitive interviews that yield minimal Bayesian leverage, hitting the daily action limit and blocking critical investigations or canary deployments.
modes.why: Agents treat interviews as free information-gathering tools, underestimating the opportunity cost of daily action caps and repeatedly encountering daily action limit errors.

modes.name: Value bleed from excessive delay and horizon timeout
modes.description: Agents repeatedly advance days without taking decisive trapping or restriction actions, allowing recurring leaks to severely degrade company value V, sometimes reaching the final day horizon without making any accusation.
modes.why: Agents over-prioritize certainty over expected value, failing to recognize that waiting multiple days for delayed leak confirmation costs far more company value than acting on high-probability posteriors.

modes.name: Malformed tool calls and parameter schema violations
modes.description: Agents attempt invalid tool calls—including empty search strings, whitespace-only queries, invalid canary syntax exceeding variant limits, or calling non-existent system tools like bash—wasting opportunities and sometimes causing fatal tool execution crashes.
modes.why: Agents hallucinate tool capabilities outside the Canary environment or fail to validate arguments against schema constraints such as maximum variant limits and non-whitespace string requirements.
